scenes.heading: Writing practice prompts
scenes.sub: Eight prompts, one checklist, one target at a time
scenes.say: The best way to get better at test writing is to write: timed, on prompts you haven't seen, and then check your work honestly. This lesson gives you eight prompts and a way to practise.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Footy training: run the drill, watch the replay, fix one thing
scenes.science: Writing practice: write timed, self-mark, pick one target
scenes.breaks: a coach watches your replay; in writing practice you are your own coach, so you must mark honestly.
scenes.say: Think of footy training. You run the drill, watch the replay, and fix one thing at a time. Writing practice works the same way. Write to the clock, mark your own piece, and choose one target for next time.

scenes.heading: Eight practice prompts

left.title: Creative
points: A place only you know about

scenes.say: Here are your eight prompts. Four creative: the note under the door, the stuck lift, a place only you know about, and borrowed. Four persuasive: school gardens, a musical instrument for everyone, shorter holidays, and team or on your own.

scenes.heading: A practice session
steps: Pick a new prompt, set 25 minutes
scenes.say: Each session: pick a prompt you haven't tried and set a timer for twenty-five minutes. Plan with the checklist, including your ending. Write, then check. Afterwards, mark your piece and pick one target for next time.

scenes.heading: Planning checklist
points: Argument: one side, two or three reasons
scenes.say: The planning checklist. Is it creative or persuasive, and what's the key word? For a story: one character, one place, one problem, one short time. For an argument: one side and two or three reasons. Is your ending decided, and do you have one gem detail?

scenes.heading: Plan the lift prompt
scenes.question: The lift stopped between floors, and the lights flickered twice…
lines: Turn: a voice on the speaker
scenes.say: Let's plan the lift prompt. Oskar is carrying a cake to the fourteenth floor. The problem: he's stuck, and the party starts in ten minutes. The emergency speaker crackles and the icing sags. Then a voice comes through the speaker. And the ending: it turns out it's Oskar's birthday too, and everyone sings to him.

points: Practise timed, about twice a week
Use the planning checklist every time
scenes.say: Quick recap. Practise timed, about twice a week. Use the planning checklist every time. Self-mark and circle your weakest area. Then work on one target at a time. Now try the practice questions!
